etymology: English: the finding relabelled as a fraud, so that the measurement becomes a motive.
effect: The capability of a funded interest to convert a measurement into an opinion: the thermometer is real, the reading is a debate, and the debate is the product.
available_to: Any interest that needs the finding to stay a controversy for one more budget cycle.
counter: Ask what would falsify it, then point at the number that has not moved. A hoax is a claim with no test; this one has forty years of them.
senses: The manufacture of doubt about a measurement: the same three contrarian papers circulated for a decade, the expert with a degree in something else, the study that is always about to be published.
It works because doubt is cheaper than denial. You do not have to win the argument, only keep it open - and an open argument is a reason to wait, which is the only policy the funder needed.
example: *"The science isn't settled" - the **climate hoax** in six words, forty years after the first consensus, by a body that had settled its own position in a memo.*

confused_with.tell: Bothsidesing gives a finding equal time with its denial; the climate hoax is the campaign that made the denial worth airing.
